evals.name: base-template
evals.prompt: Scaffold me a Go API template with routing, env config, CORS, JSON helpers, Postgres, migrations and auth. Module github.com/dimamaimesko/starter.
evals.expected_output: A runnable Go JSON API project with module github.com/dimamaimesko/starter: routing, configuration from the environment, CORS restricted to trusted origins, JSON read/write helpers with JSON errors, a PostgreSQL connection pool, up/down SQL migrations and working register/login/protected-route auth.
expectations: The project is a Go module named github.com/dimamaimesko/starter
go build ./... and go vet ./... pass
staticcheck reports no problems
gofmt reports no unformatted files
go.mod has no web framework, ORM, query builder, or config/logging library
Migrations are up/down SQL pairs that apply, fully roll back and re-apply on an empty PostgreSQL database
Configuration comes from environment variables listed in a .env.example (or equivalent), with no hard-coded database credentials in Go code
The API starts against PostgreSQL and its healthcheck returns 200 with a JSON body
Auth works end to end: a user can register and log in to get a token, and a protected endpoint returns 401 without the token and 2xx with it
CORS answers only configured origins (no wildcard) and handles preflight requests
Unknown routes and wrong methods return JSON 404/405, and a malformed JSON body returns 400 with a clear message
Passwords are stored hashed (bcrypt or argon2) and auth tokens are not stored in plaintext
The server shuts down gracefully on SIGINT/SIGTERM
The README explains setup, configuration and the endpoints

evals.name: bookstore-api
evals.prompt: Create a bookstore API in ./bookstore (module github.com/dimamaimesko/bookstore) with books: title, author, isbn, price, published year. Anyone logged in can read, only staff can edit.
evals.expected_output: A runnable Go JSON API in ./bookstore with users and token auth, a books resource (title, author, isbn, price, published year) with create/list/show/update/delete, where any logged-in user can read and only staff can write.
expectations: The project is in ./bookstore and is a Go module named github.com/dimamaimesko/bookstore
go build ./... and go vet ./... pass
staticcheck reports no problems
gofmt reports no unformatted files
go.mod has no web framework, ORM, query builder, or config/logging library
Migrations are up/down SQL pairs that apply, fully roll back and re-apply on an empty PostgreSQL database
No leftover template example code or placeholders (no items resource, example.com/app or APP_ variables)
Books have create, list, show, update and delete endpoints with title, author, isbn, price and published year
Unauthenticated requests to the book endpoints get 401
A logged-in user without staff rights can list and read books but gets 403 when creating, updating or deleting
A staff user can create, update and delete books
Invalid book input (such as a missing title, malformed ISBN, negative price or future year) is rejected with 422 or 400 and per-field messages
Price is not stored as a floating-point number (integer cents or NUMERIC)
Updates are protected against lost concurrent edits (a version column or equivalent)
The list endpoint supports pagination

evals.name: greenlight-reviews
evals.prompt: Add reviews to greenlight: a user can post a review (rating 1-5 and text) for a movie, list a movie's reviews, and delete their own.
evals.expected_output: Changes to the existing greenlight project that add movie reviews (create, list for a movie, delete own) following the project's existing conventions, with new migrations and docs.
expectations: go build ./... and go vet ./... pass
staticcheck reports no problems
gofmt reports no unformatted files
No new third-party dependencies were added to go.mod
Existing migrations are unchanged and the new ones are up/down pairs numbered after 000006
All migrations apply, fully roll back and re-apply on an empty PostgreSQL database
An authenticated, activated user can post a review for an existing movie, and a rating outside 1-5 or missing text gets 422
Posting a review for a movie that doesn't exist returns 404
A movie's reviews can be listed
A user can delete their own review; deleting another user's review is refused (403 or 404) and the review remains

The change follows the project's conventions: envelope responses, helpers from cmd/api/errors.go, a model in internal/data with value semantics and per-query timeouts, and routes registered in routes.go with the existing auth wrappers
The README or docs/openapi.yaml documents the new review endpoints
Existing movie endpoints still work
